stage: stage1-v5 preliminary body and interface preflight
scope: Before freezing preliminary body, materials and mount law for three separate canonical component reviews. Twelve representative native renders only. No final 576-frame image approval or canonical equipment/family/cover approval.

observations.assessment: The native hull is substantially rounder and more cohesive than the old faceted source. Red pods have constructed bands and end caps; the porthole has a substantial flange, gasket and fasteners. Fins, nose lights, status fixture and propeller remain recognizable at logical size. All four directions form a coherent vehicle. Old topology and part counts were not treated as requirements.

Warm gold/yellow body, coral red pods, blue porthole and restrained dark/silver fittings separate clearly on light, gray and dark backgrounds. Broad soft shading avoids the original blown yellow facets. One symmetric cardinal light rig and neutral registered camera are retained; no directional target highlight was required. The visible result is somewhat less glossy and more golden than the target, which is acceptable except for the focal glass issue below.

Pod bands, porthole trim and mechanical fixtures read at 320×384 logical and 160×192 display size. Provisional upgrades remain distinct enough to demonstrate placement and silhouette without certifying their final design. Baseline mounting pads are understood as physical seats, not canonical armor art.

Supplied native family views keep the ship distinct from the hut, preserve its dock placement and source-like modest hover. The physical family uses the disclosed main 65° camera on a larger canvas, rather than pretending to match separately registered 55° companion sprites. No grounded-skid demand or future cover-clearance inference was made.

blockers.location: The main blue porthole in all four baseline and provisional upgraded representatives, most evident in dock-ready-S.png and the logical-size comparison sheets.
blockers.issue: The large blue window reads as a softly shaded, nearly uniform opaque blue disc. Its rim shows construction, but the window itself has weak glass depth and reflection cues. This loses a prominent material distinction and focal feature of the fixed target; at logical and smaller display sizes it still reads more like a blue painted insert than convincing glass.
blockers.desiredOutcome: Give the native blue porthole a clearly readable sense of depth and controlled reflection/highlight or edge-value separation, coherent across all four facings under the same symmetric light/material recipe. Preserve the vivid blue area and substantial rim; exact target glint positions, directional lighting, literal transparency or copied photographic detail are not required.
blockers.whyBeforeFreeze: The porthole belongs to the preliminary main body/material set that will become immutable while canonical components are tuned. Resolve this visible body-material issue before sealing that set.
blockers.scope: A focused native body/material refinement; no change to registered root/camera, animation semantics, hover role or proposed component transforms is requested.

technicalPreflight.status: No hard technical blocker found for this partial checkpoint. Mount reservations are feasible proposals, not approval of future component geometry.

Verdict is based on actual pixels.

Supplied actual-floor hover .0370000005–.0730000138 stays inside frozen .02–.09. Hut conservative disjoint-X gap .32725 canonical S and .273 fixed-root/all-body-facing are positive. This judge did not separately rerun the complete floor BVH batch in this checkpoint.
technicalPreflight.portableReproduction: Portable recipe, clean-build native identity report/log, full reopened-source replay log, face-order normalization evidence and calibrated replay deltas inspected. Reports retain up to 2/255 in at most 7 pixels for v5 same-order comparisons; no fake universal raster identity required. technicalPreflight.partialScope: Only the supplied twelve primary representative images, their comparison sheets and two independent replay representatives were visually reviewed. Missing final 576 native images/48 atlases is explicitly pending after canonical adoption, not a Stage1 evidence failure.

componentFreezeAssessment.physicalMounts: Actual saved local matrices match proposed positive uniform scales .5/.35/.4 and declared translations; legacy attachment-base keys and coordinates remain unchanged. No per-view or nonuniform scaling is proposed.
componentFreezeAssessment.finiteSeatEvidence: Independent evaluated finite contact faces saved in independent-interface-audit.json. Panel top patches are X[-.249,-.181] and [.181,.249], Y[.028,.292], Z .65. Harpoon top patch X[.2695,.3505], Y[-.1955,-.0445], Z .5685. Collector front bracket face is Y−.454, X±.117, Z[.1665,.2575]. These finite surfaces are smaller than the broad beveled seat AABBs and should travel with the frozen mount law. Collector rear engagement is an intentional structural overlap, not a promised empty air gap.
componentFreezeAssessment.reservationClearance: Proposed neutral occupied regions separate from the glass/periscope/propeller and unrelated equipment as documented; split panel side regions, not their combined empty central AABB, establish the periscope corridor. This leaves a viable interface basis without locking current provisional part counts or appearance.
componentFreezeAssessment.projectionTradeoff: Main 65° square-pixel capture and component 55.00798°/pixelAspect1.22065556 captures remain distinct. Proposed saddle pair is wider and flatter than old single hull-panel object; harpoon base is narrower with a longer occupied envelope; collector is wider and shallower. All four neutral reservation projections fit fixed standalone frames without camera fitting. Actual canonical art, small-scale readability, contact contouring and all standalone active frames remain for fresh component judges.
componentFreezeAssessment.consumerRole: These standalone objects are catalog comparison assets, while the main upgraded variant adopts their neutral native geometry/materials at the once-frozen transforms. No separate raster overlay, new active-main mapping, effect binding, statistic or gameplay mechanic is inferred.
componentFreezeAssessment.recommendation: Retain the proposed geometric interface basis and the staged adoption plan. Revise the focal glass appearance, then return exact revised body/material bytes for a bounded Stage1 recheck before the coordinator freezes the body and component mount law.

acceptedDifferences: No exact target rivet count, panel-line density or single-view highlight direction is required.
A somewhat more golden and restrained finish than the target is acceptable when focal material readability is resolved.
Provisional cannon, paired plates and intake are placement/clearance evidence; their final canonical art is pending.
Current family evidence certifies no future cover, final accepted companion publication or final consumer sprite composition.
